title: Stable Diffusion – much faster!
reading: The slide introduces Stable Diffusion as a latent diffusion model: the diffusion process is applied in the latent space rather than pixel space, and it is presented as the first large-scale, open-sourced text-to-image generative model. The canonical latent diffusion architecture figure from Rombach et al. occupies the lower portion, annotated in red to separate the image-to-latent encoding stage from the diffusion stage. The citation Rombach et al., CVPR 2022 appears at the bottom.

visuals.description: Latent diffusion architecture: pixel space (pink) with encoder E mapping x to z and decoder D producing x̃; latent space (green) containing the diffusion process producing z_T and a denoising U-Net ε_θ with repeated ×(T−1) denoising steps and cross-attention Q/KV blocks; conditioning panel (grey) with semantic map, text, representations, images fed through τ_θ. Legend shows denoising step, crossattention, switch, skip connection, concat. Red overlay boxes label 'Image to latent' (top) and 'Diffusion model in the latent space' (bottom).
visuals.assertion: An autoencoder compresses images to a latent code where the conditioned denoising U-Net runs diffusion, so generation is cheaper than operating on pixels; conditioning enters via cross-attention from a domain encoder τ_θ.
